b: Better than ever before, the latest album by the British electronic trio captures the thrill and spontaneity of their live sets

Last month, I exchanged emails with Nik Colk Void about a piece for this website on the enduring influence of Daphne Oram, during which Void wrote eloquently about the importance of live settings for her work with sound. “Continuing to insist that new musical languages can be invented through direct, imaginative engagement with sound [is] something I often experience in a live context,” she wrote. “The room and the audience become part of my decision-making process, influencing how a composition develops.”
